summary.name: NVBeacon
summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu bar app that monitors remote NVIDIA GPU servers over SSH using nvidia-smi.
use_cases: Watch a remote GPU server's load from the macOS menu bar
Get notified when a long-running GPU training process exits
Find an idle GPU to use for the next job
Check which users and processes are using each GPU without opening a shell
Set up remote GPU monitoring from ~/.ssh/config hosts
summary.what_it_does: NVBeacon runs in the macOS menu bar and connects to a remote GPU server over SSH, using nvidia-smi to report live GPU utilization. A compact popover shows per-GPU process details including user, PID, GPU memory, and a command preview. Users can track specific processes and receive a native notification when they exit, and star GPUs to get alerts when they have been idle for a long period. Configurable busy detection rules and an option to import SSH targets from ~/.ssh/config are included. The page says the UI is available in English and Korean and supports light, dark, and system appearance.
notable: Per-GPU process detail (user, PID, GPU memory, command preview) without keeping a shell open
Process exit and GPU idle notifications
Imports SSH targets from ~/.ssh/config; supports key-based or password-based auth
Open source, listed in awesome-mac under Menu Bar Tools
caveats: Requires an SSH-reachable remote server with nvidia-smi; the page is for NVIDIA GPUs only
Pricing is not stated on the page; the awesome-mac listing describes it as freeware and open source
